Simulation: Estimating M with One Monotone Anchor per Ordering

Ziang Zhang

Question

How accurately does the current MPCurver automatic-\(M\) workflow recover the number of latent sample orderings when each ordering has one monotone anchor and all remaining trajectories are smooth and nonmonotone?

We fitted all 90 fixed datasets with MPCurver 0.3.4 using fit_mpcurve(intrinsic_dim = "auto"). The final effective \(M\) is exact in 88/90 datasets. The two errors are underestimates in the hardest \(M=5\) settings; there are no final overestimates. Mean feature-partition ARI is 0.994, and mean matched ordering recovery is 0.839.

Simulation design

Each dataset contains 300 samples and 60 features, arranged in balanced groups following 3, 4, or 5 independent latent orderings. This gives 20, 15, or 12 features per ordering. For sample \(i\) and feature \(j\),

\[X_{ij}=f_j(t_{i,z_j})+\epsilon_{ij},\]

where \(z_j\) identifies the feature’s ordering and the latent positions are independent Uniform\((0,1)\) draws. Within each group, one feature is a monotone anchor. Every other feature follows a random smooth mixture,

\[f_j(t)=\sum_{k=2}^{4} \frac{a_{jk}\sin(k\pi t)+b_{jk}\cos(k\pi t)}{k^2},\]

where the coefficients are independent standard normal draws. Retained curves have derivatives of both signs on a 1,001-point grid, so every non-anchor trajectory contains at least one change of direction. Each noiseless feature is centered and scaled to sample variance one.

The variance signal-to-noise ratio is 1, 4, or 16, with 10 independent datasets per condition. The feature groups are balanced, and the simulation does not include garbage features.

Simulated trajectories and observations

The following figures show replicate 1 from every condition. Each row is a true ordering and each column is an SNR setting. Blue shows the monotone anchor; orange and purple show two nonmonotone trajectories in the same group.

Methods

Automatic dimension initialization

MPCurver 0.3.4 computes a directional nonlinear similarity for every feature pair. One feature is sorted, and the other is regressed on its normalized rank with a natural cubic spline having five fixed degrees of freedom. The score is the proportion of response variance explained; the symmetric similarity is the larger score from the two directions.

Single-linkage clustering considers cuts with at most eight groups. A cut is eligible only when every group contains at least two features. Among eligible cuts, the selected initial \(M\) maximizes mean silhouette width. If the selected group sizes are \(d_1,\ldots,d_M\), adaptive EB starts with the global assignment probabilities

\[p(z_j=m)=d_m/60.\]

The tree cut therefore initializes the number and relative sizes of the orderings without imposing a hard feature assignment. Adaptive EB may remove components during fitting.

Ordering and fitting

Isomap is applied independently within every selected feature group to initialize its sample ordering. Coordinate-ascent variational inference (CAVI) then fits 50 position-grid points, a second-order random-walk prior with ridge = 0, adaptive cell-position priors, estimated feature-specific noise and smoothness, and annealing from temperature five to one. Convergence requires absolute ELBO change divided by \(ND\) below \(10^{-6}\), with at most 10,000 sweeps.

The reported effective M is the number of components whose mean posterior feature-assignment probability exceeds \(10^{-12}\). Feature-group recovery uses the adjusted Rand index (ARI). Ordering recovery matches occupied inferred orderings one-to-one with the true orderings by absolute Spearman correlation, allowing reversal; an unmatched true ordering contributes zero.

All results below use MPCurver 0.3.4, commit 15f2b0bbe5dfa61cd46da5160b2bc251e75a0475.

Recovery of M

The spline-similarity cut selects the true initial \(M\) in 88/90 datasets, with 0 underestimates and 2 overestimates. After adaptive EB, the effective \(M\) is exact in 88/90, with 2 underestimates and 0 overestimates.

Recovery of the underlying structure

The current fit has mean feature-partition ARI 0.994. Its mean matched ordering score is 0.839. Feature grouping is nearly exact even at SNR 1, whereas estimation of the continuous sample positions is more sensitive to noise.

Runtime and convergence

All 90 current-package fits converged without fitting warnings. Median single-thread runtime is 34.6 seconds per dataset. Runtime includes similarity calculation, automatic dimension selection, ordering initialization, annealing, and adaptive fitting.

Median single-thread runtime of MPCurver 0.3.4 automatic-M adaptive fitting. Each point summarizes 10 complete fits, including similarity calculation, dimension initialization, and adaptive EB.

Summary and reproduction

On these balanced one-anchor datasets, the current MPCurver workflow recovers the final effective ordering count in 88/90 datasets and never overestimates it. The two misses combine two true orderings in the hardest \(M=5\) settings. Feature groups remain nearly exact overall; continuous ordering recovery improves sharply with SNR.

This design assumes at least two features per ordering, includes one monotone anchor in every group, and contains no garbage features. The minimum-cluster rule prevents singleton orderings but does not identify unstructured features; that requires a separate background or garbage component.

The experiment directory contains all 90 fixed inputs, saved fits, validation records, result tables, current-package figures, and reproduction scripts. The frozen MPCurver 0.3.4 source archive has SHA-256 58d0c99c6170994c82eedba190fb1c28a63eb47530c575705323c3cf3992b7c6.
